chapter: Sunset Cafe, Pass in Review and rebuilding the band
title: Organizing the second band for Armstrong; Canetti and the copied scores
summary: After Armstrong's return from Europe Randolph put a band together; the booker Canetti held Armstrong's music, so Bobby Wall copied Randolph's scores and Glaser hocked the Sunset for uniforms.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: About when was this, Mr. Randolph? '33, '34?
This -- yeah, sometimes I get those years mixed up.
Let's see. The Century of Progress was in 1933, I believe, wasn't it? The exposition?
'33, '34. This must be '33. Yes, I believe this was '33, when I organized the band.
When you organized the second band for Louis, I think it was in January of '33 when he came back to Chicago. And then that band stayed together for about six months, according to what I've read.
Canetti
Yeah, that was --
And this must have been after that.

It was after that, because I remember when it came back to Louis and I was telling him all the scores, different scores that I had -- I think [Cossetti] had took Louis' -- do you know anything about that? [Cossetti] took Louis' music, to keep Louis -- see, when Louis got ready to leave, [Cossetti] --
[Cossetti], the booker?
Yeah, he was the booker over in France or something like that.
Oh.

And he took Louis' music and Louis didn't have a bit of music. So when Louis came back, and I was naming all the arrangements that I had, scores, but they wasn't copied, and he says, "You got all these arrangements, Randy?" I told him Yes.
So we hired this little fellow, Bobby [Wall], to do the copying. I don't know (inaudible), where Bobb he'll tell you -- you might know Bobby through the Cats and the Fiddles, or something.
Oh, yes.

He was the violin player in that outfit at that time, when they had the Cats and the Fiddles, but I think they had broken up when he was writing for me. Or copying, you know, copying my arrangements. Because it was
Canetti

a heck of a job to get the arrangements ready, to get the band out, because I know Joe had to -- yeah, I remember him hocking the Sunset to get the uniforms, to get the band equipped and everything, to get out.
This was when Louis came back from France.
From France, yes.
In the '35 band that you put together for him.
Yes, yes, but -- well, I would say '34, I believe.
'34 he put the band --
Uh-huh. '34, because we were with this outfit during '33 and when it was over with Louis came back, and I got the band together for Louis.
